themes.title: Anthropic drops Claude 5.5 family, files for IPO
themes.summary: Anthropic shipped a full Claude 5.5 refresh (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) with meaningful price-performance gains — Opus 5.5 costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 — and filed an S-1 for a proposed IPO, a first for a frontier lab. The move makes agentic coding and knowledge work cheaper at the exact moment DeepSeek is coming after Claude Code.
themes.angle: Inference unit economics, not model specs, is the new competitive frontier — and the IPO filing signals the sector's shift to capital-markets discipline.

items.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5 Claude Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge work, and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.
items.note: Flagship lands 40% cheaper to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads, per Anthropic.

items.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5 Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a clear upgrade over Claude Sonnet 5, runs 30%+ faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work.
items.note: Workhorse tier: 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper than Sonnet 5, per Anthropic.

items.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 Claude Haiku 5.5 is our fastest, most capable small model. Built for high-volume work like summarization, subagents, and browser use.
items.note: Fastest small model, pitched at summarization, subagents and browser use.

themes.title: Aramco takes 49% of HUMAIN in $2.6B AI deal
themes.summary: Saudi Aramco acquired 49% of PIF-backed AI firm HUMAIN for $2.6B in cash plus AI assets, with PIF retaining 51%. HUMAIN is targeting 3GW of AI data-center capacity by 2030 — the clearest sign yet that Saudi sovereign capital is consolidating its AI infrastructure play under one national champion.
themes.angle: A template for GCC sovereign AI: energy major + sovereign wealth fund + a single national compute champion.

themes.title: The agentic coding arms race
themes.summary: DeepSeek shipped a prototype autonomous coding agent targeting Anthropic's Claude Code, while Anthropic open-sourced its agent skills via a new foundation. Agent-mediated commerce is also taking shape, with publishers experimenting with ads shown only to AI agents.
themes.angle: Coding agents are becoming a product market with real unit economics — relevant to every AI-native SDLC decision.

themes.title: Compute economics cools the capex narrative
themes.summary: Kioxia's 15% slide signals memory demand leveling after the AI surge, and Google's energy chief poured cold water on space data centers (up to 100x cost). The hardware narrative is moving from scarcity toward unit economics.
themes.angle: Contrarian read: the AI capex supercycle may be turning into a normal supply-demand curve.
